newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Builder Solel Boneh to issue shares in Tel Aviv.
newsitem.headline: Builder Solel Boneh to issue shares in Tel Aviv.

text.p: Israel's leading construction contractor, Solel Boneh Building & Infrastructure Ltd, said on Sunday it would hold an initial public offering (IPO) on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in early June.
It said in a statement it intended to raise 79 million shekels ($23.2 million) immediately through a combined issue of shares, convertible bonds and warrants.
It expects to raise a further 130 million shekels from the exercise of the warrants and conversion of the bonds -- 18 million shekels in six months and 112 million within two years.

The offering will value the company at a minimum of 420 million shekels, Solel Boneh said. Its equity capital at the end of March totalled 160 million shekels and it paid a dividend of 33 million shekels in 1996.
Solel Boneh, a subsidiary of the Housing & Construction Holding Co, had net profit of 60 million shekels in 1996 and more than 21 million shekels in the first quarter of 1997.

In 1995-96 it had annual turnover of 1.85 billion shekels, against 1.45 billion a year in 1993-94. Its order backlog, according to the company's prospectus, rose to 1.9 billion shekels at the end of April from 1.7 billion at the start of 1996.
Among the projects it is involved in is the building of the Hyatt hotel at the Dead Sea, which will bring Solel Boneh 97 million shekels in revenue.

"The Solel Boneh bourse issue presents another step in the plan for public offerings for the entire Housing & Construction group after the sale of the parent company to its workers was completed successfully," Uzi Vardy-Zer, Solel Boneh chairman and Housing & Construction managing director, said in a statement.
Housing & Construction is 72.7 percent owned by its workers and 21.9 percent owned by Arison Investments, the Israeli investment arm of billionaire businessman Ted Arison.
Solel Boneh had cancelled plans for an IPO in 1994 when share prices on the Tel Aviv market plunged.
Its latest endeavour comes amid a revival of the new issues market in Tel Aviv following a rally in stock prices that began at the end of last year.
Many real estate companies are making offerings while the government is raising 1.2 billion shekels from shares and warrants in Bank Leumi and Israel Discount Bank.
Analysts estimate 15 to 20 companies are planning Tel Aviv offers.
